steps.text: Place chocolate chips into a glass or metal bowl, and set over the top of a pan of barely simmering water. Stir occasionally until melted and smooth. Remove from the heat and transfer chocolate to a medium bowl.
Add sour cream and vanilla; beat with an electric mixer until smooth and creamy. If you let it cool down too much, it will set up; so frost your cake while it is still liquid, or reheat before using.

raw_recipe.headline: Sour Cream Ganache
raw_recipe.description: This ganache makes a super easy frosting that is great for when you have leftover sour cream in the fridge and chocolate chips on hand — delicious over almond-flavored cupcakes!
raw_recipe.name: Sour Cream Ganache

review.reviewBody: I was looking for a recipe for classic ganache to top a chocolate cheesecake with and came across this recipe. Since sweetened sour cream is a classic plain cheescake topping I gave this one a try for my chocolate cheesecake. It was the PERFECT compliment to the rich cheesecake. Dense but not too heavy and sweet but refreshing in compliment to the intense chocolate of the cheesecake. EXCELLENT - thanks for a great recipe!

I thought this was very good! I used Nestle vanilla chips to go with a chocolate fudge cake mix and about 1- 1/2 Tblsp of Dekuyper buttershots liqueur while melting the chips. Could also just mix the liqueur with the sour cream before mixing all together. Could not taste the sour cream flavor at all. I cored out the middle of the cupcakes and poured the Ganache inside, then let them sit in the fridge overnight. I will make these again!

I made this to add onto the top of my chocolate chip banana bread. It was amazing. I did add a little sweet cream butter to the chocolate chips while melting them. Then after I mixed in the sour cream I added a small pinch of powdered sugar and cocoa powder. Turned out SO delicious!

I was looking for a substitute for whipping cream in ganache and found this recipe. I used 60% bittersweet dark chocolate chips melted in the microwave. I knew it might be too sour for my tastes so I added 1/3 cup powdered sugar to the sour cream before combining it with the melted chocolate. It was a nice topping for my chocolate cheesecake. I also added chopped Oreo cookie pieces on top of the ganache before chilling. I liked it well enough to make this again.

Jan. 2016 (Football party in Downs): halved recipe... mixed 1/2 c. Sour cream, 1/4 c. Heavy cream, 1 Tbs powedered sugar - heat in microwave til hot; add 1 c. Semi sweet chips and 1 tsp vanilla - stir til smooth, pour over cooled brownies.
Oct. 2016 (NASCAR party in Downs): I heated the sour cream in the microwave and then stirred the chips in until melted; then stirred in vanilla. Next time I'll add some sugar to sweeten or use half semi-sweet and half milk chocolate chips.

5 stars as a chocolate cheesecake topping. I agree that the sour cream could be tasted, but it was a great compliment to the cheesecake! It was very easy to make in the microwave. I just stirred every 10 seconds until it was perfectly smooth. So easy!
Only made half the recipe and it easily covered 2 dozen cupcakes. I melted the chocolate in the microwave and used the full teaspoon of vanilla so it was easier to spread.

OH. MY. GOSH. Tangy and chocolatey is a sensation! And no butter. I didn't bother getting out the mixer or messing up a bowl. Melt chocolate in a pot, add SC and vanilla and whisked. The recipe makes A LOT. Actually, too much. I halved the recipe and it was still too much for 1 bundt. Next time, I'll try cutting down to 1/3.

I made this because I had made it before years ago to put on cheesecake. So lovely! It has a shine to it that is so pretty. I think you should add the sour cream in and taste as you go so that you do not get the sour taste you do not like. That is different for everyone so it is a good excuse to sample as you are adding. Yum! Anyway, I loved this on Black Magic Cake from this site. I also added some peppermint extract to make a mint chocolate cake. Super YUM! Here's to death by chocolate!

I made this but had to make some changes to the recipe because the flavor was odd. I followed the instructions exactly and was pleased with the texture, which was beautiful, but the flavor was sour and bitter with an aftertaste of chocolate. I added one more teaspoon of vanilla and about a tablespoon of honey which definitely helped. If I make it again I will experiment with reducing the sour cream or using milk instead of semi sweet chips.

I Have made this many times and always turns out great for me I like the less sweet flavor the sour cream gives this. I didn't change anything. I have used semi sweet and milk chocolate chips (not together two different batches) both come out great.
Really lovely flavor and so easy to ice a cake using it.

My sister taught me to make this in the 70s. It’s the only frosting I make other than cream cheese. Just pulled this up just to revisit the portions of sour cream and chocolate chip. Truly Excellent, best served having been refrigerated overnight. This could not be easier to make. So rich!

I used yogurt instead of sour cream and it tasted nice. I used semi sweet chocolate chips and added a few white chocolate chips to make it a bit sweeter. I wish I had known how to make this years ago! How did I miss this recipe!
Yum!
This on top of triple chocolate molten lava cupcakes was WONDERFUL. It balanced the super sweet cupcakes nicely without making them too sweet. Quick and easy too
We thought this was perfect with One Bowl Chocolate Cake III!
BEST FROSTING EVER!
Meh, I followed the recipe. I think it's too bitter but maybe it's supposed to be

Love this ganache. Have used it for years. I hate buttercream frostings but love this ganache. It is not a favorite of children or adults who like sweet icings/frostings. As it sits, it darkens and gets shiny. Simple ganache with ingredients easily found in your kitchen.
